newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper opens sharply down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper opens sharply down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper furtures continued the week's falls to open sharply down on Thursday after copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) showed no signs of stopping losses overnight, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract opened at 22,000 yuan ($2,654) per tonne, down 280 yuan from Wednesday's close. It moved around that level early in the session.

A wave of speculative selling swept through the LME on Wednesday, driving prices to the lowest levels for seven weeks, with the benchmark three months delivery price falling to $2,355 at one stage during hectic trading, down $82 from Tuesday.
Last three months business was at $2,373 a tonne, still down a hefty $64 from Tuesday's close.
Traders in Shanghai said the weak performance on the LME triggered more stop-loss orders on the local market, but short-covering at low levels prevented further falls.
They said they expected the market to remain steady for the rest of the session.
The price of physical copper was around 22,100 to 22,300 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, compared with 22,500 to 22,600 yuan on Wednesday.
Aluminium opened mixed. July fell 10 yuan to 13,500 and August rose 70 yuan to 13,700 in the early morning session.
